title: EDF-Based Mixed-Criticality Scheduling with Graceful Degradation by Bounded Lateness

extraction.paper_name: EDF-Based Mixed-Criticality Scheduling with Graceful Degradation by Bounded Lateness
extraction.paper_description: This paper introduces MCQOS-schedulability, a framework for mixed-criticality systems that guarantees bounded lateness for a subset of low-criticality tasks (QOS-tasks) during high-criticality mode, rather than dropping them entirely. It proposes the EDF-VDS algorithm, which uses virtual deadlines and a server task to manage these guarantees.

formal_description.statement: A HI-task tau_i is defined by (C_LO_i, C_HI_i, T_i) and a LO-task by (C_i, T_i). Utilizations are defined as: u_HI_i = C_HI_i / T_i, u_LO_i = C_LO_i / T_i, and u_i = C_i / T_i. Aggregated utilizations are U_HI_HI = sum(u_HI_i for tau_i in T_HI), U_LO_HI = sum(u_LO_i for tau_i in T_HI), U_LO = sum(u_i for tau_i in T_LO), and U_QOS = sum(u_i for tau_i in T_QOS).

variables.C_LO_i: Optimistic worst-case execution time of HI-task i
variables.C_HI_i: Pessimistic worst-case execution time of HI-task i
variables.C_i: Worst-case execution time of LO-task i
variables.T_i: Minimum inter-arrival time (period) of task i
variables.U_HI_HI: Total utilization of HI-tasks in HI-mode
variables.U_LO_HI: Total utilization of HI-tasks in LO-mode
variables.U_QOS: Total utilization of the QOS-task subset

formal_description.conclusion: Establishes the basic workload metrics for mixed-criticality analysis.

informal_sketch.intuition: Defines how much processor time each task and group of tasks requires under different criticality assumptions.
steps: Calculate individual task utilizations for both HI and LO scenarios.
Sum utilizations based on task criticality sets (T_HI, T_LO, T_QOS).
Ensure the system is not fundamentally overutilized in either mode.
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def get_utilizations(T_HI, T_LO, T_QOS):
    U_HI_HI = sum(t.C_HI / t.T for t in T_HI)
    U_LO_HI = sum(t.C_LO / t.T for t in T_HI)
    U_LO = sum(t.C / t.T for t in T_LO)
    U_QOS = sum(t.C / t.T for t in T_QOS)
    return U_HI_HI, U_LO_HI, U_LO, U_QOS
key_insights: U_QOS represents the persistent load from low-criticality tasks that must be maintained even in HI-mode.

formal_description.statement: A system is MCQOS-schedulable if: 1) In LO-mode (all jobs <= optimistic WCET), all deadlines are met. 2) In HI-mode (some HI-job > C_LO_i), all HI-tasks meet deadlines and all QOS-tasks (tau_i in T_QOS) have bounded lateness.
assumptions: Jobs exceeding C_HI_i or LO-jobs (not in T_QOS) exceeding C_i are considered erroneous.
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the correctness criteria for graceful degradation.

informal_sketch.intuition: Extends standard MC-schedulability by requiring that QOS-tasks are not dropped but instead guaranteed to finish within a fixed delay after their deadlines.
steps: Monitor job execution times.
If a HI-job exceeds C_LO_i, switch to HI-mode.
In HI-mode, ensure HI-tasks meet deadlines and QOS-tasks eventually finish.
key_insights: Lateness (finish_time - deadline) must be bounded by a constant for QOS-tasks.

formal_description.statement: For a HI-task tau_i, the virtual deadline is T_prime_i = x * T_i, where x = U_LO_HI / (1 - U_LO). The schedulability test is x * U_LO + U_HI_HI <= 1.
formal_description.conclusion: Provides the basis for the LO-mode scheduling of EDF-VDS.

informal_sketch.intuition: Shrink HI-task deadlines in LO-mode to create a 'buffer' that allows the system to handle the increased load during a mode switch.
steps: Calculate the shrinking factor x based on system utilizations.
Assign virtual deadlines to HI-tasks for LO-mode scheduling.
Verify the utilization-based sufficient test.
key_insights: Virtual deadlines prioritize HI-tasks in LO-mode to ensure they are 'ahead of schedule' if a switch occurs.

formal_description.statement: Upon mode switch at t_1: 1) Drop T_LO \ T_QOS. 2) Schedule HI-tasks by EDF until t_2 (first HI-idle instant). 3) At t_2, introduce server task tau_QOS with period T_QOS and budget C_QOS = U_QOS * T_QOS. Schedule tau_QOS and HI-tasks together via EDF.

variables.t_2: First HI-task idle instant after t_1
variables.T_QOS: Tunable period of the server task
variables.C_QOS: Execution budget of the server task

assumptions: tau_QOS executes pending QOS-jobs using its budget.
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the runtime behavior for graceful degradation.

informal_sketch.intuition: After a mode switch, first clear the immediate HI-task backlog, then use a periodic server to provide a guaranteed share of the processor to the remaining LO-tasks.
steps: At t_1, stop all non-QOS LO-tasks.
Run HI-tasks until the processor would naturally be idle (t_2).
From t_2 onwards, treat the QOS workload as a single periodic task with utilization U_QOS.
The server task tau_QOS picks the earliest-deadline QOS job to run.
key_insights: The server task tau_QOS abstracts the entire QOS task set into a single periodic entity for the EDF scheduler.

formal_description.statement: Property 1: For any interval delta, supply S(delta) >= (delta - 2 * (1 - U_QOS) * T_QOS) * U_QOS. Property 2: For an interval delta starting at t_2, S(delta) >= (delta - (1 - U_QOS) * T_QOS) * U_QOS.
assumptions: The server task tau_QOS meets all its deadlines (guaranteed if U_HI_HI + U_QOS <= 1).
formal_description.conclusion: Provides lower bounds on the execution time available to QOS-tasks.

informal_sketch.intuition: The server task behaves like a periodic resource. These properties quantify the 'worst-case' amount of time the server gets to run within any window.
steps: Identify the worst-case alignment of server jobs within a window delta.
Calculate the minimum execution time (supply) based on the periodic resource model.
key_insights: The 'blackout' period is the time the server is not running within its period.

formal_description.statement: Lemma 1: If a QOS-idle instant exists in [t_2, f], lateness L <= 2 * (1 - U_QOS) * T_QOS. Lemma 2: If no QOS-idle instant exists, L <= (t_2 - t_1) + sum(C_i for tau_i in T_QOS) / U_QOS + (1 - U_QOS) * T_QOS.

variables.f: Finish time of a QOS job
variables.sum_C_QOS: Sum of WCETs of all QOS tasks

formal_description.conclusion: Bounds lateness for two exhaustive scenarios of processor demand.

informal_sketch.intuition: Lateness is caused either by the server's own periodicity (Case 1) or by the initial backlog of HI-tasks and QOS-tasks after the mode switch (Case 2).
steps: Case 1: The server is occasionally idle, so lateness is limited by the server's maximum 'off' time.
Case 2: The server is constantly busy, so lateness depends on the time taken to clear the accumulated workload.
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def calculate_case_lateness(t1, t2, T_QOS_tasks, U_QOS, T_server):
    # Case 1
    L1 = 2 * (1 - U_QOS) * T_server
    # Case 2
    sum_C_QOS = sum(t.C for t in T_QOS_tasks)
    L2 = (t2 - t1) + (sum_C_QOS / U_QOS) + (1 - U_QOS) * T_server
    return L1, L2
key_insights: The term (t_2 - t_1) represents the 'HI-task interference' window where QOS tasks are blocked.

formal_description.statement: If a system is MC-schedulable under EDF-VD and U_HI_HI + U_QOS <= 1, then all HI-task deadlines are met under EDF-VDS.
formal_description.conclusion: Guarantees that adding QOS support does not compromise high-criticality tasks.

informal_sketch.intuition: Since the server task tau_QOS only starts after the HI-task backlog is cleared (at t_2) and the total utilization is <= 1, standard EDF theory ensures no deadlines are missed.
steps: Verify LO-mode via EDF-VD.
Verify HI-mode by checking if the combined utilization of HI-tasks and the server task is <= 1.
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def is_hi_task_safe(U_HI_HI, U_QOS, edf_vd_passed):
    return edf_vd_passed and (U_HI_HI + U_QOS <= 1)
key_insights: The delay in starting the server (until t_2) is crucial for HI-task safety.

formal_description.statement: The lateness of any QOS-task in HI-mode under EDF-VDS is bounded by: L_max = (1 - U_QOS) * T_QOS + max((1 - U_QOS) * T_QOS, (2 * sum(C_HI_i for tau_i in T_HI)) / (1 - U_HI_HI) + sum(C_i for tau_i in T_QOS) / U_QOS).

variables.sum_C_HI: Total pessimistic WCET of HI tasks

formal_description.conclusion: Provides a closed-form guarantee for the degraded performance of LO-tasks.

informal_sketch.intuition: Combines the bounds from Lemma 1 and Lemma 2, using a worst-case estimate for the duration of the HI-only interval (t_2 - t_1).
steps: Calculate the maximum duration of the HI-mode busy period (t_2 - t_1).
Apply the case analysis from Lemmas 1 and 2.
Take the maximum of the two cases to find the global bound.
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def get_lateness_bound(T_HI, T_QOS_tasks, U_QOS, T_server):
    U_HI_HI = sum(t.C_HI / t.T for t in T_HI)
    sum_C_HI = sum(t.C_HI for t in T_HI)
    sum_C_QOS = sum(t.C for t in T_QOS_tasks)
    
    t2_t1_max = (2 * sum_C_HI) / (1 - U_HI_HI)
    
    term_common = (1 - U_QOS) * T_server
    case1 = term_common
    case2 = t2_t1_max + (sum_C_QOS / U_QOS)
    
    return term_common + max(case1, case2)
key_insights: Lateness is sensitive to the server period T_QOS; smaller periods reduce the bound but increase overhead.

formal_description.statement: Any system where U_HI_HI + U_QOS > 1 cannot be MCQOS-schedulable under any algorithm.
formal_description.conclusion: Establishes the fundamental limit for providing lateness guarantees in MC systems.

informal_sketch.intuition: If the total required utilization in HI-mode exceeds 100%, the backlog of work will grow infinitely, leading to unbounded lateness.
steps: Assume U_HI_HI + U_QOS > 1.
Observe that no jobs from these sets are dropped.
Conclude that demand exceeds supply, making bounded lateness impossible.
key_insights: Graceful degradation still requires that the 'essential' HI-mode workload is feasible on a single processor.
